captions.caption: The screen is black.
A close-up shot shows the long barrel of an M777 howitzer against a cloudy sky.
The camera pans down the barrel of the howitzer in a snowy field.
The camera continues to pan down, revealing the breech mechanism of the artillery piece.
As the camera pans, soldiers in camouflage uniforms and helmets come into view.
The shot reveals the full side profile of the M777 howitzer and its crew.
The artillery crew is positioned around the weapon under a large camouflage net.
A soldier in the foreground adjusts their gear while others operate the howitzer.
The sun shines brightly behind the soldiers and the artillery piece.
The soldiers continue their preparations around the large artillery piece.
A close-up shot shows the frosted base of a green artillery shell.
The camera tilts up along the body of the frosted artillery shell.
The camera continues to pan up the shell, with wooden crates and a tire in the background.
The camera focuses on the top cone of the artillery shell, which has a yellow barcode sticker.
A soldier wearing black gloves places a fuze on the tip of the shell.
The soldier's hands are shown firmly holding the shell's fuze in place.
The soldier finishes setting the fuze on the projectile.
A row of green 155mm artillery shells is shown lined up on wooden pallets.
The camera focuses on the yellow stenciled markings on the side of the shells.
The markings indicate the shells are 155H Projectile M795 with TNT.
A close-up view of the lot numbers and other identification marks on the projectiles.
A low-angle, wide shot shows the howitzer's muzzle brake covered in frost.
The howitzer is positioned under a camouflage net in a frosty field.
The entire howitzer is visible, appearing cold and frosted over in the early morning light.
The sun glints off the frosted surface of the artillery piece.
The scene remains static, showing the prepared and frosted howitzer.
A soldier in a balaclava takes a large, cylindrical propellant charge from a stack on a truck.
The soldier carefully pulls the propellant charge tube from the honeycomb-like rack.
He continues to pull the long tube out from the pallet on the truck.
The soldier lowers the propellant charge from the truck bed.
He holds the large, white tube containing the propellant and turns.
The soldier prepares to hand the propellant charge to another soldier on the truck.
He hands the propellant charge up to a soldier standing on the truck bed.
The soldier on the truck takes the charge and turns toward the rack.
The soldier places the propellant charge into an empty slot on the rack.
Another soldier is seen helping secure the load on the truck.
The two soldiers work together to organize the propellant charges on the truck.
A wide shot shows the artillery crew working around the howitzer under a camouflage net.
A commander begins to shout orders to the crew.
The soldiers move quickly to prepare the weapon for a firing mission.
Orders for a 10-round mission with HE shells are shouted.
The crew continues to prepare, with empty propellant tubes scattered on the ground.
Soldiers are actively working on the howitzer's controls and loading mechanism.
The commander continues to call out firing data to the gun crew.
The commander calls out the charge number for the mission.
The crew members are all focused on their specific tasks around the gun.
The soldiers acknowledge the orders while continuing to work.
The commander calls out the deflection for the artillery piece.
A closer view from under the net shows a soldier operating the howitzer's controls.
Soldiers move around the gun, adjusting settings based on the shouted orders.
A soldier in the background runs to get more equipment.
A low-angle shot from behind the howitzer shows the crew moving in the mud.
Soldiers quickly move around the base of the artillery piece.
One soldier carries a heavy projectile towards the breech of the gun.
The crew works in unison to load the heavy shell into the howitzer.
A soldier uses a ramming staff to push the projectile completely into the breech.
Another soldier prepares the propellant charge to be loaded next.
The shell is loaded, and a soldier confirms it aloud.
The crew continues to work on the breech and prepare for firing.
A soldier closes the breech of the howitzer after the shell and charge are loaded.
